baseline.note: Chief complaint: Persistent cough for ~1 week, worse at night, mostly dry with occasional clear sputum in the morning. History: No fever, occasional shivering, mild exertional dyspnea (climbing stairs), no chest pain. Past medical history: Childhood pneumonia, otherwise healthy. Social: Former smoker (10 pack-years, quit 5 years ago). Medications: Cetirizine 10 mg for seasonal allergic rhinitis. Allergies: No known drug allergies. Family history: Mother with asthma, brother recent chest infection. Review of systems: Negative except cough and mild dyspnea. Physical exam: Temp 37.1°C, SpO2 97% on room air. Throat mildly erythematous. Lung auscultation: mild bilateral wheezes on expiration, no crackles. Assessment: Likely viral upper respiratory infection or post‑viral cough; no clear signs of bacterial chest infection. Plan: Reassure, supportive care, monitor symptoms, advise to return if worsening dyspnea or new fever, consider trial of a cough suppressant if needed, continue cetirizine for allergy symptoms.
